newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA UNDECIDED ABOUT WENGEN SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA UNDECIDED ABOUT WENGEN SLALOM.

text.p: Alberto Tomba, insisting he is unconcerned about tumbling out of the World Cup giant slalom top 15 rankings for the first time in 10 years, is recovering from flu but may still skip Sunday's slalom in Wengen.
The world and former Olympic champion told Italian newspapers he would be leaving for Madonna di Campiglio on Wednesday to pick up his training programme again.
"But I still don't know whether I will be at the start at Wengen on Sunday," he was quoted as saying in the Gazzetta dello Sport. "I need to be well and in good physical shape."
"On Sunday in Chamonix I should not have started but I wanted to see what kind of strength I had."
However Tuttosport newspaper, quoting the Italian's coach Gustavo Thoeni, said Tomba aimed to be at Wengen.
Tomba, who crashed heavily in pre-season training and injured a wrist and knee, has struggled to get back to his old form and has only completed two races this season.

The Italian, who captured both the giant and slalom world titles in Spain last year, was second in a slalom on his season's debut at Madonna before Christmas but failed to finish a giant slalom in Kranjska Gora, Slovenia, on January 5.
He was eighth in a slalom there the next day.
He also crashed out of a special three-legged exhibition slalom in Sestriere, on the piste where the world championships will be held next month, on New Year's day.
At Chamonix in France last weekend the triple Olympic champion was second fastest in the first leg of a slalom before pulling out with flu without racing the second leg.

His absence from Tuesday's giant in Adelboden, the last giant before Sestriere, knocked Tomba out of the top 15 seeded skiers -- meaning that he will not be able to draw a start number in the giant slalom at the championships.
"It's not a big problem," the Italian said from his home at Castel de Britti near Bologna.
"In the giant its not as important to be among the first starters as it is in the slalom, where you have to find the tightest possible line and go very close to the gates.
"If the piste is in good shape, as it certainly will be at Sestriere unless we get bad weather, there will be no problem.
"In the giant you can clock very fast times even with the 20th start number."
Tomba, who has been taken care of by his mother at the family home, said the most important thing was that he should get his fitness back in time for Sestriere.
"I am training a bit, the wrist is better and in Chamonix I was able to push a bit harder. But I know I will have to carry that pain for a bit longer. It's the flu that worries me."
